newsitem.title: UK: Golden Vale '96 profits drop, outlook tough.
newsitem.headline: Golden Vale '96 profits drop, outlook tough.

text.p: Irish food group Golden Vale Plc on Tuesday posted a sharp drop in 1996 profits and said the outlook for this year remained tough.
Golden Vale's 1996 adjusted pretax profit dropped to 7.9 million punts, before a 1.6 million charge, compared to 16.1 million a year earlier.
Turnover dipped to 561 million punts ($869.5 million) from 564 million.
The company proposed a final dividend of 1.6 pence per share, making a total payout of 2.26 pence for the year, unchanged from the 1995 level.
"In general, the outlook for 1997 remains tough," the company said, adding that it would focus on improving profits in its cheese business and reducing its cost base, among other goals.
Golden Vale said the performance of its butter and milk powders business would continue to depend on imbalances between market prices for the products and the price paid for milk.
Despite what it called a "disappointing profit performance" for the year, Golden Vale managed to reduce its gearing to 60 percent at December 31 compared to 78 percent a year earlier.
Total debt was currently about 60.9 million punts.
Following the withdrawal of certain court proceedings against it, the company cancelled about 9.0 million ordinary shares held in a trust pending the resolution of the proceedings, Golden Vale said.
The issued share capital after the cancellation was about 157.5 million shares.
